newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end off lows after rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end off lows after rate decision.

text.p: Tel Aviv shares closed only moderately lower on Tuesday, despite disappointment over the Bank of Israel's decision to leave interest rates unchanged, traders said.
"We were expecting a much sharper decline today following the interest rate decision," said Uri Schur of Eyal Securities.
On Monday, after the market's close, the central bank said it would keep its key lending rate unchanged for December at an annualised 15.2 percent.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 0.49 percent, or 0.97 points, to 195.82 on an all-share turnover of 76 million shekels against 60 million on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 0.33 percent to 205.56.

The Mishtanim index was down more than one percent by early afternoon, but staged a partial recovery by close. Most trading activity was in the Maof shares, with foreign investors noticably active, said Izik Winish of Capital Securities.
"Towards the end of the day the mood in the market changed completely. The options market reflects expectations that the market will resume its rise on Wednesday," Schur said.

"The reaction to the rate announcement was very moderate and investors are very optimistic now," said Winish. "After two days of profit-taking the market is ready for another rise. Most investors believe that in the short run the positive trend will continue."

Clal Industries, the day's most active share, gained 0.5 percent to 1,346 on volume of 4.7 million shekels. Clal reported a third-quarter net loss of 54.9 million shekels against net profit of 71.0 million shekels a year earlier. Traders said the results were within expectations.
However, Clal's parent company Clal Israel lost 1.0 percent to 7,274.
The Israel Corp dropped 3.75 percent to 17,984 after two of its group companies, Israel Oil Refineries and Zim Israel Navigation, published lower-than-expected third-quarter earnings.

Oil Refineries had third-quarter net loss of 6.7 million shekels against net profit of 29.4 million shekels a year earlier. For the same periods Zim reported a net loss of $6.3 million against net profit of $5.3 million.

Elbit, dropped 4.0 percent to 13,641, which traders attributed to profit-taking after a sharp rise in the last month. Elbit said on Monday it had completed its break-up into three separate publicly traded companies.

Other active shares included Koor Industries, which lost 0.75 percent to 28,233 on volume of 3.9 million shekels, and Bezeq Israel Telecom which closed unchanged at 777 on turnover of 2.4 million shekels.
